content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp price spikes.
- Forecasts tend to be too high in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window, then gradually adjust — suggesting a lag in recognizing short-term volatility.
- After a price spike, model forecasts overshoot and remain elevated longer than true prices, indicating failure to capture mean reversion.
- Model underestimates prices in the final 5–10 days of the forecast horizon, particularly when true prices show upward momentum.
- Forecasts exhibit a persistent upward bias in the middle of the 30-day window, especially when historical prices are trending downward.
- Model fails to adjust for sudden downward corrections in the last 5–10 days, leading to overestimation of future prices.
- Forecasts are overly smooth, missing sharp reversals or sudden spikes in true prices — suggesting lack of sensitivity to volatility clustering.
- Model tends to overreact to recent high prices, leading to prolonged overestimation even after prices begin to decline.
